scenes.headline: How a model that can't type runs web tasks
scenes.sub: Jev plus Mercury 2.5 over WebMCP, on WindTunnel's 21-configuration board.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Caramel! Jev can only pick from a list. It can't write a single word. Paired with a writer, it tops a web-agent board. Here's how.

scenes.text: Split the agent in two: a decision model picks the site's tool, and a small writer fills in its arguments. Neither does the other's job.
scenes.say: The idea: split the agent in two. A decision model picks the tool, and a small writer fills in the arguments. Jev never types, and Mercury never chooses.

steps.say: Under WebMCP, the page registers its own tools. Those tools, plus finish and abstain, become the menu.
Jev reads the state and picks one option. That's all it can do: choose, with a probability for each.
Mercury, a fast diffusion model, writes the arguments, forced into the chosen tool's own schema.
If an argument is wrong, a well-built tool replies with the legal values, and the next step uses one.

left.title: Driving the page
items: The menu is the page's numbered controls
Every click is its own decision
left.say: Driving the page, every click is a separate decision. A checkout takes a median of twenty-two actions.

right.title: Calling WebMCP tools
items: The menu is the site's registered tools
One call can hold a whole journey
right.say: With tools, one call can hold a whole journey. The same checkout takes four.

scenes.title: Taking the headline apart
scenes.say: The headline: two hundred and forty-five times cheaper than GPT-6 Astra on screenshots. But two things changed at once.

parts.note: Astra alone, on WebMCP instead of screenshots
parts.say: About fifteen of it is the interface: Astra itself, moved to WebMCP, mostly reading less.

parts.note: same interface, a cheaper pair per token
parts.say: About sixteen is price: the same interface, with a pair that costs far less per token.

scenes.text: Most of the margin is the interface, available to any model that uses it. The decision model wins on price per token.

recap: Jev picks the tool; Mercury writes arguments
Tools compress a journey into one call
scenes.say: To recap: one model picks, one types, tools compress the journey, and the big multiplier is two smaller ones.
